title: Trilateral Commission North America finance and institutional-history pass, 2026-08-08
summary: Depth-3 audit of the North American legal/financial entity, recent Form 990 trends, regional fundraising, founding aims, and historical grant support.

sources.title: Trilateral Commission North America - Nonprofit Explorer
Contributors' identities not subject to disclosure

evidence.observation: EIN 23-7309933 is reported for Trilateral Commission North America. FY2025 data reports revenue $792,627, expenses $1,839,874, net income -$1,047,247, net assets $895,435, and contributions $749,531 (94.6% of revenue).
The FY2025 filing index lists Richard Fontaine as Executive Director with $125,000 compensation.
The Commission describes North American fundraising as decentralized and says U.S. support includes corporations, foundations, and individuals.
The Rockefeller Archive Center finding aid documents a policy-recommendation function, the 1972 formation process, and early Rockefeller/Kettering/Ford support.
Rockefeller Brothers Fund states that it made grants to the Trilateral Commission during its 1970s international-program work.
IRS guidance says contributor names and addresses for ordinary exempt organizations generally are not required to be publicly disclosed.

gaps: Full FY2025 Form 990 and Schedule O field extraction remains.
Canadian and Mexican legal entities remain unresolved.
Named current donors require donor-side disclosure research.
caveats: Four consecutive deficits and reserve drawdown do not by themselves establish financial distress.
Historical funding must not be presented as current without current evidence.
North American filings must not be attributed to Europe or Asia Pacific without legal-identity evidence.

provenance.method: public tax filing, official history, IRS disclosure, and archival-source audit

workflow.next_action: Model the North American legal entity through repository scripts, then invert-search donor-side filings and reconcile trustees/officers.

notes: Model Trilateral Commission North America separately for U.S. tax and governance data.
FY2025 was contribution-dominated and reported a large deficit after deficits in FY2022-FY2024; this is a trend requiring explanation, not proof of distress.
Primary archival sources document policy-recommendation aims and early Rockefeller/Kettering/Ford financing.
Recipient Form 990 review cannot yield a complete current donor list; use donor-side disclosures.

classification_rules: Separate regional legal entities and tax filings from the global membership organization unless legal identity is established.
Represent annual financial values as time-scoped observations.
Do not infer financial distress from deficits alone.
Treat historical grant support as historical unless current evidence establishes continuation.
Use donor-side filings and explicit grant records for named funding edges.
data.method: Compared FY2022-FY2025 IRS-derived financial data with Commission regional funding language, IRS disclosure rules, and Rockefeller archival/foundation histories.
data.narrative_role: legal-entity resolution, financial trend audit, funding provenance, and institutional history
data.research_question: What legal and financial entity operates the North American group, what do recent public filings establish, and what can primary archival sources establish about founding aims and funding?

findings.finding: Trilateral Commission North America has a distinct U.S. tax identity, EIN 23-7309933.
FY2025 finances were overwhelmingly contribution-funded and substantially expense-negative.
Negative net income is reported for FY2022 through FY2025.
Richard Fontaine's North American executive-director role is independently corroborated by filing data.
Primary archival sources document a policy-recommendation function and early Rockefeller/Kettering/Ford financing.
Rockefeller Brothers Fund confirms historical grant support.
A complete present-day donor list cannot be extracted from recipient-side public Form 990 records.
